newsitem.title: USA: Unimed's nitazoxanide drug trial positive.
newsitem.headline: Unimed's nitazoxanide drug trial positive.

text.p: Unimed Pharmaceuticals Inc said on Wednesday its new drug, nitazoxanide (NZT), showed positive Phase II trial results in treating cryptosporidial diarrhea, a potentially life-threatening complication of AIDS.
There is no consistently effective or approved therapy for cryptosporidiosis, which is caused by a microscopic parasite, the company said in a statement.
It is estimated that 15 to 20 percent of AIDS patients suffer from this condition, Unimed said.

"Within three to five years of launching NTZ, we estimate it will have sales in the range of $50 million to $100 million in the United States, Canada, Australia and New Zealand," President and Chief Executive Officer Steve Simes told Reuters.
Unimed has a license to develop and market the product in these four countries, Simes said.
He said the company hopes to launch the product by early 1998 and a Phase III trial is planned to begin by year-end.

In people with normal immune function, cryptosporidiosis generally lasts up to two to four weeks, Unimed said. The company estimated 45 million people in the United States could be exposed to drinking water from systems contaminated with cryptosporidium.
